e2e-23191782-season-7686105.title: Two public readers treat a normally-produced manifest as malformed: `verify` cannot exit 0 on any real archive (append-only history -> `manifest_duplicate_work_id` -> unrecognised -> `structural_input_error` -> `0 if not defects and not diagnostics` fails), and plain `coverage` loses its denominator entirely (`manifest_state` forced to "malformed" -> `denominator_available = False` -> count None / state "unavailable"). A third reader, `coverage --quality`, applies no such override and reports the same archive fine — so the readers disagree with each other about one input.
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.source: E2E run e2e-23191782-season-7686105 (2026-09-17), finding F6 in {WORKFLOW_DIR}/e2e-23191782-season-7686105/reports/e2e.md; extended 2026-09-17 by the register review that measured all three readers against the same archive. Decisive probes, on one fully-archived healthy row / the season root: `verify --trusted-local --scope BV1RFoxBqEzo:p0 --format text` -> `checked: 1 / defects: 0 / diagnostic: structural_input_error / EXIT=1`; `coverage --format json` -> `denominator {count: None, state: 'unavailable'}, exit 1`; `coverage --quality --format json` -> `denominator {count: 39, state: 'available'}` on the same root.
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.scope: One emitter and three readers of the same projection. Emitter: src/bili_asr/sidecar_projection.py L216 raises `manifest_duplicate_work_id` for ordinary append-only state history (needs_audio -> audio_ok -> archived). Readers, all via `project_manifest_records`: (1) src/bili_asr/integrity.py L203 — the recognised-diagnostic vocabulary at L205-232 omits the string, so the else-branch maps it to `structural_input_error`, and cli.py's exit rule `0 if not payload['defects'] and not payload['diagnostics']` turns it into exit 1; (2) src/bili_asr/coverage_report.py L65 + the override at L76-77 — forces `manifest_state = "malformed"`, which at L198 makes `denominator_available` False and blanks every coverage ratio (L223-224 `count None` / `state "unavailable"`); (3) cli.py L1264 (the `--quality` branch) — no override, so its denominator is correct (39 / available). Note coverage_report.py L325 *also* files the same string as a benign record-kind diagnostic, so one file treats it as both a record fact and a malformation. Test blind spot unchanged: tests/test_integrity.py::test_production_archive_layout_verifies_cleanly writes exactly one row per work_id and asserts only `defects == []`, never the diagnostics set or the exit code.
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.target: the next plan that touches src/bili_asr/integrity.py or src/bili_asr/coverage_report.py — and the first thing to settle is not the code but the definition: **is append-only state history well-formed?** The `--quality` branch already answers yes (it applies no override), so the cheapest consistent fix is to adopt that answer in both other readers — drop the malformed override in coverage_report.py L76-77 and either recognise the diagnostic in integrity.py or stop emitting it for ordinary history. Then pin the exit contract with a fixture whose manifest carries a real state history (two rows for one work_id), which no current fixture does. Any plan that gates CI on `verify` is blocked on this.
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.tracking: Registered here, and materially EXTENDED on 2026-09-17 during the register review: the original entry described only `verify`'s exit contract, which understated the blast radius — plain `coverage` is broken by the same root cause and loses its denominator, while `coverage --quality` is fine. One fix closes both, so this stayed a single row rather than becoming two entries for one cause. Severity held at high rather than raised to critical: two public readers misreport on every real archive (a false red on the integrity gate and the completeness report), but nothing is corrupted, no data is lost, and `recover` is unaffected because `authoritative` is computed from attempt diagnostics only (integrity.py L233-236). Measured universality unchanged: 15 of the season's 39 work_ids carry 2-3 rows, all appended by the product's own paths, and the deleted 2026-09-12 batch manifest had the same shape.

e2e-23191782-season-7686105.title: Latin tokens glue inside a cue when Nano omits their leading space: `_token_cues` builds the cue text with `"".join(parts)`, while the space-repair rule (`_join_text`) is applied only when absorbing an undersized cue and when handing a closing mark back — so the third place that needs it, intra-cue concatenation, glue words together (measured: 'asME IDEA', 'bothAND', 'questionITSELF', 'anITEM').
e2e-23191782-season-7686105.source: Deep text-quality pass over the season run's 14 archives, 2026-09-17 ({WORKFLOW_DIR}/e2e-23191782-season-7686105/reports/e2e.md, text-quality section). e2e-23191782-season-7686105.scope: bilibili-asr-archive/src/bili_asr/asr.py _token_cues: `parts.append(piece)` + `text = _clean_text(pending + "".join(parts))` versus `_join_text`, which is called only from `hand_back()` and from the undersized-cue absorption path. `_join_text`'s own docstring already declares the phenomenon and the rule ('Nano emits an English phrase as several tokens and does not always carry the leading space'), so this is the rule applied in two of the three places it is needed. Candidate fixtures: pytest's tmp_path and any session/module-scoped fixture in conftest.py.
